component.name: Foresight
component.summary: Preview and run rsync transfers with a dry-run change list

description.p: Foresight is a GNOME-native front-end for rsync. Every sync starts as a preview: a real dry run, rendered as a grouped list of changes — created, updated, deleted, and attributes-only — so a mistake is obvious before a single byte moves.

ul.li: Grouped change preview from a real rsync dry run before every transfer
Add files and folders from different locations as sources, or drop them in
Live transfer view with a progress bar and a structured activity log
Mirror deletions (--delete) gated behind a confirmation of exactly what would be removed
Advanced options: move, unit-aware bandwidth limit, ordered include/exclude filter rules, and free-form extra arguments
Remote sync over SSH: push to or pull from another machine, authenticated by your desktop's SSH agent
Reusable presets for your Advanced-option sets
An honest, in-app inventory of exactly which rsync flags this build exposes

description.p: The rsync engine is bundled and version-pinned, and all file access flows through desktop portals — Foresight never asks for your whole home directory.

screenshot.caption: Configure a job: add sources and a destination
Preview every change, grouped, before it runs
Advanced options: move, bandwidth limit, filter rules, and extra flags
Sync to another machine over SSH, using the keys in your agent
An honest, in-app list of what Foresight can do

description.p: Two fixes from a month of daily use, and a newer rsync.

ul.li: After a transfer to or from a remote machine, New Job left both remote buttons greyed out, so no further job could be started without restarting Foresight. Fixed.

An exclude rule that can never match is now pointed out. A rule beginning with / is matched from the top of the transfer, not the top of the disk, so a full path pasted as an exclude matched nothing — and said nothing. With Move on, the folder it was meant to keep back was moved along with everything else. Nothing was lost, but it was not where you expected. Such a rule now shows a warning, and a Fix button with the rule that was meant.
A dry run now reports what each filter rule matched, and names any that matched nothing.
With Move on, Foresight checks first and asks before starting if an exclude rule is not holding anything back.
The bundled rsync is now 3.5.0, which fixes a large number of security issues.

description.p: Remote sync over SSH, and filter rules you can order. This is 1.0: everything Foresight advertises now works, and the formats it saves are stable.

ul.li: Sync to or from another machine over SSH. Either the source or the destination can be on a remote host — rsync does not allow both.
Authentication uses the keys already in your desktop's SSH agent. No private key ever enters Foresight's sandbox, and your ~/.ssh is never read.

Foresight keeps its own record of the hosts you trust and shows you a machine's fingerprint before connecting to it the first time. After that, a host key that does not match stops the transfer instead of being accepted quietly.

Exclude patterns became an ordered list of Include and Exclude rules. rsync obeys the first rule that matches, so moving a rule up or down decides which one wins: an Include above a broad Exclude carves an exception out of it, and an Exclude above an Include shuts a folder even to that.
When a remote transfer fails, the reason SSH gave is now shown with the failure rather than only in the log.
Presets saved by any earlier version still load.

description.p: An exclude-rule editor, and a fix for presets that quietly failed to save.

ul.li: Exclude patterns are now a managed list — one row per rule, each with its own remove button, added by typing a rule and pressing Enter.
A rule may contain spaces. The old single field split on whitespace, so a rule like "My Documents/" became two rules and matched nothing.

Fixed: a preset whose name contained a square bracket, tab or line break was silently discarded when saved. It appeared to save, worked for the rest of the session, and was gone at the next launch. Any name can now be stored.
Presets saved by earlier versions load unchanged and are migrated the next time they are saved.

description.p: Fixes where a folder lands in the destination.

ul.li: A folder you add now arrives in the destination as that folder. Previously a lone folder had its contents copied loose into the destination, so they spilled in alongside whatever was already there.
The old behaviour is still available, but now you have to ask for it: Advanced, Sync folder contents. It applies only when the job has exactly one folder as its source.
The What Foresight Can Do dialog explains where your files land.
Preview any sync as a grouped change list — created, updated, deleted, attributes-only — from a real dry run.
Add files and folders from several locations to one job, by browsing or by drag and drop.
Live transfer with a progress bar, current-file label, a structured streaming log, and cancel.
Mirror deletions asks you to confirm the exact list of files it will remove.
Advanced options — move, bandwidth limit, excludes, extra arguments — saveable as presets.
A What Foresight Can Do dialog listing every rsync flag this build exposes, alongside the bundled rsync's own help.

description.p: Ships sandboxed, reaching your files only through portals, with rsync 3.4.4 bundled and version-pinned.
